rawCandidates.title: Obsidian rotate chat command can permanently delete review-vault files without authorization, confirmation, or destructive audit
rawCandidates.source: Any chat user who can invoke /plur1bus can supply obsidian rotate --apply --delete --allow-delete plus age/size options.
rawCandidates.control: runPlur1busCommand dispatches every obsidian action to handleObsidianBridgeCommand at index.js:2948-2983 before calling checkAuth; the rotate branch treats the two flags as sufficient approval and has no user/chat-bound confirmation nonce.
rawCandidates.sink: rotateOldArchives reaches unlinkSync(f.path) at lib/obsidian/archive-rotation.js:156-160 for matching top-level .json, .md, or .txt files beneath the configured review root.
rawCandidates.impact: A non-whitelisted user in a shared chat can permanently remove review/control-room artifacts and evidence despite a configured PLUR1BUS whitelist; the operation is not recoverable from an in-command archive and leaves no appendDestructiveOpLog receipt.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Static reachability is direct and the plugin's other destructive routes call checkAuth, making this branch an enforcement outlier. Validation should execute the registered command handler with configured allowedUserIds excluding the caller and a temporary review root containing an old Markdown file, first proving dry-run safety and then proving the explicit delete flags remove it without invoking confirmation/audit callbacks.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Preconditions are access to a chat where /plur1bus commands are registered, a writable configured review root, and a matching old/oversize top-level supported-extension file. Traversal and symlink defenses constrain the target set, but they do not restore caller authorization. A feature-preserving fix is to require the existing user/chat authorization and bound confirmation flow while retaining move, delete, and dry-run modes.

notes: One destructive-command candidate. The archive engine itself correctly defaults to dry-run and contains paths; the defect is the missing chat authorization/confirmation/audit boundary, so remediation need not remove or disable rotation.
